investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the pod's affinity or selector at all. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims found, every remote agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable before the VM is provisioned. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this scheduling blockage: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers the pod creation that then stalls, so no evidence is ever written back to satisfy the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never scheduled.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before VM provisioning.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers remote pod scheduling — the failure occurs at or immediately after this call.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. If the affinity rules are overly narrow (e.g., targeting a specific node pool or label that only 2 nodes carry), expanding the eligible node set could resolve the issue.

TERTIARY — insufficient node pool size for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class: the cluster may not have enough nodes provisioned with the kata peer-pods runtime to absorb concurrent remote agent creation requests from the observability probes plus any live workloads.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource shows available capacity on the two affinity-matching nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., a quota, taint, or toleration mismatch) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the probe immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the issue was transient (e.g., a briefly held vm slot was released) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to match more than 2 of the 6 nodes, the '4 node(s) didn't match' message would indicate a label drift or node configuration change rather than an intentionally narrow selector.

If stale pods from prior probe runs are found to be holding vm slots and are cleaned up, and subsequent probes succeed, the root cause would be a probe cleanup regression rather than a hard capacity limit.
If the cluster has only 2 nodes provisioned with the kata peer-pods runtime and both are at their vm slot limit, the issue is a provisioning/scaling gap rather than a configuration error.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all nodes in the remote-agents node pool, alerting before slots are fully exhausted rather than only after a pod fails to schedule.

Add a stale-pod detection eval that counts remote agent pods older than a configurable TTL (e.g., 10 minutes) that are still consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, to catch cleanup regressions before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 3), to catch node label drift or pool shrinkage early.
Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run check (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) as a lightweight canary eval that can detect Unschedulable conditions without actually consuming vm slots.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion prevents pod scheduling across all three remote-agent checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~143 s before the check timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature eval in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-level failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the peer-pod VM quota is fully consumed, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods. All three sibling checks report the same message, confirming this is a shared infrastructure constraint rather than a per-check code defect (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or misconfigured, expanding the eligible node pool could resolve scheduling even without adding VM quota.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent VM was ever provisioned, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a Kubernetes scheduling constraint failure; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod could not be placed: 0/6 nodes were available — 2 reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no preemption victims found on the 2 eligible nodes; preemption not helpful on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes). The pod remained unscheduled for 147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a complete contract gap across all 5 required fields.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner produced zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not match the pod's affinity or selector at all. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims found, every remote agent pod request is rejected as Unschedulable before the VM is provisioned. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this scheduling blockage: the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885 calls createAgent with machineType "remote", which triggers the pod creation that then stalls, so no evidence is ever written back to satisfy the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 254–259.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduling failure message, pod stuck for 147s, latencyMs=151958 — same root cause reproduced on a third independent probe attempt.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — the runner never reached the point of writing orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState because the pod never scheduled.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before VM provisioning.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers remote pod scheduling — the failure occurs at or immediately after this call.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never started.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-matching nodes: all allocatable peer-pod VM slots on those nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's affinity/selector rules restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. If the affinity rules are overly narrow (e.g., targeting a specific node pool or label that only 2 nodes carry), expanding the eligible node set could resolve the issue.

TERTIARY — insufficient node pool size for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource class: the cluster may not have enough nodes provisioned with the kata peer-pods runtime to absorb concurrent remote agent creation requests from the observability probes plus any live workloads.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dry-run check (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) as a lightweight canary eval that can detect Unschedulable conditions without actually consuming vm slots.

Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) never returned an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, the eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~143 s before the check timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature eval in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this is an eval-level failure, not a confirmed user-facing outage.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent VM was ever provisioned, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a Kubernetes scheduling constraint failure; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the resulting pod could not be placed: 0/6 nodes were available — 2 reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no preemption victims found on the 2 eligible nodes; preemption not helpful on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes). The pod remained unscheduled for 147 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a complete contract gap across all 5 required fields.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: expected-output contract at lines 266-269 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running VM.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible swarm nodes: existing remote agent VMs from prior runs or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Tertiary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes never match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the effective scheduling pool is always limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have a small VM quota, any concurrent workload can exhaust capacity. This is a structural constraint that amplifies the impact of any resource leak.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the number of concurrent or lingering eval pods, independent of any cleanup issue.

affectedAreas.label: Kubernetes swarm node pool — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message explicitly names 2 nodes with Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm as the blocking constraint. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Remote agent pod scheduling — node affinity/selector rules
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, permanently restricting the schedulable pool to 2 nodes and making the system fragile to any VM slot exhaustion (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — remote agent creation path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at lines 1913-1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers the pod that fails to schedule. The eval cannot proceed past this point without a running VM (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract — remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') are unmet because the agent VM was never provisioned (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence, source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270).

affectedAreas.label: Feature registry — remote-agents feature checks
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks registered under remote-agents (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed. The feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2, meaning two required-check failures (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) satisfy the outage threshold (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189).

recommendedNextActions: Check current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot usage on the 2 eligible swarm nodes immediately. If slots are fully occupied, identify and terminate any orphaned remote agent pods or VMs from prior eval runs to restore scheduling capacity.

Verify that the withCleanup wrapper in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs correctly deletes remote agent resources on both success and failure paths, including error/timeout scenarios. If cleanup is not guaranteed on timeout, add a finally-block or equivalent safeguard.

Review the node affinity and selector configuration for remote agent pods. With only 2 of 6 nodes eligible, the effective VM quota is structurally limited. Consider whether additional nodes can be labeled to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm or whether the quota on existing nodes can be increased.

Monitor the remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) after any remediation to confirm they return to passing. The feature registry shows degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2; both required checks have already failed, satisfying the outage threshold.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies any orphaned pods from prior eval runs that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and were not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (evidence: source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node affinity and selector rules on the remote agent pod spec
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms why 4 of 6 nodes are permanently ineligible and whether the affinity rules can be relaxed to expand the schedulable pool (evidence: failed-check.message — '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector').

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes shows available capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or quota enforcement issue would need to be investigated.

If no orphaned remote agent pods or VMs are found in the cluster from prior eval runs, the cleanup-leak hypothesis (possible cause 2) would be disproved, pointing instead to concurrent external workloads or under-provisioning.

If the remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime checks pass on an immediate re-run without any cluster intervention, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a persistent resource leak.

If local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime checks also failed at the same time, the failure scope would be broader than the remote swarm node pool and would implicate a shared upstream dependency (e.g., API auth or org resolution).
If the node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to reduce the eligible node pool below 2, that configuration change — not VM exhaustion — would be the primary cause.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks available kata.peerpods.io/vm slot count on eligible swarm nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity message rather than waiting for pod scheduling timeout.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote agent pods or VMs from the current eval run remain in the cluster after the withCleanup wrapper completes.

Add a swarm node eligibility eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting if the eligible pool shrinks unexpectedly.
Consider a canary eval that runs remote-agent-create alone on a short interval (e.g., every 10 minutes) to detect VM slot exhaustion earlier, before the full runtime chain is attempted.
